experiments.title: Pay Together: Unified UPI Money Pooling
experiments.description: Architected a fintech application allowing friends to create pool groups via a unified UPI. Features included seamless payment sharing, real-time group settlement, and spending analytics. Project development was successfully modeled but eventually halted due to stringent NPCI and RBI regulatory frameworks.
story: **The Genesis:** Pay Together was born out of the universal frustration of managing group expenses manually. Whether it was splitting dinner bills, sharing rent, or funding group trips, we realized that the existing process of one person fronting the cost and painstakingly tracking down payments was broken.

**The Problem It Solves:** Traditional split-bill apps only track IOUs, leaving the actual settlement up to the users. We envisioned a radical shift: an app where friends could dynamically create a 'pool group' directly linked to a unified UPI ID. By pooling funds upfront or settling instantly via UPI, we eliminated the awkwardness of asking for money and ensured everyone paid their fair share in real-time.

**Enabling the Payment Infrastructure:** To make this a reality, we engineered a robust backend leveraging Node.js and PostgreSQL to handle complex ledger mathematics and concurrent group transactions. The core innovation was integrating with a Unified UPI API Gateway, which allowed our application to provision dynamic virtual UPI endpoints for each pool group. This meant the app could programmatically intercept incoming payments, update the group ledger in milliseconds, and securely route the final settlements—creating a truly automated, shared payment infrastructure.

**The Pivot:** Despite successfully modeling the architecture and proving out the payment flow, we eventually hit regulatory roadblocks. Stringent regulations from the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) surrounding pooled accounts and peer-to-peer lending without specialized licenses forced us to halt full-scale deployment.
